claims.statement: The 2024-03 HO-3 Section II Coverage E pays damages for which an insured is legally liable because of bodily injury or property damage caused by an occurrence and provides a defense for covered claims or suits; Coverage E applies to an insured location and personal activities, applies separately to each insured, and does not increase the applicable limit through that separation.

HO-3 Section II Coverage F provides no-fault medical-payments coverage for necessary medical expenses from accidental bodily injury, including specified injuries away from an insured location, while its business exclusion preserves only activities ordinarily incidental to nonbusiness pursuits and its animal-away-from-location grant excludes animals used in connection with a business.

The HO-3 baseline Section II exclusions remove bodily injury and property damage arising from a business or business pursuit and separately constrain business-use vehicles, watercraft, and animals, subject to the stated incidental-to-nonbusiness exception.

HO 04 42 provides attached-endorsement coverage for an insured's bodily injury, property damage, or personal injury liability arising from an occurrence connected with a lawful incidental occupancy at premises used with the residence, where the occupancy is subordinate to residential use and does not materially change the premises' residential character; it provides a defense until the applicable limit is paid or coverage does not apply.

HO 04 42 uses the policy's insured status rather than expanding who is insured, and it excludes incidental occupancy away from the residence and numerous professional, care, product, employment, vehicle, equipment, pollution, disease, intentional-act, and criminal-act exposures; it also excludes unpermitted or non-residentially subordinate business activity.

HO 04 42's W.4–W.7 grant covers bodily-injury, property-damage, and personal-injury liability and a defense subject to the applicable limit; its later W.2 section addresses covered property damage and property limits rather than adding a new liability limit, while W.30–W.38 impose prompt-notice, legal-paper, cooperation, inspection, evidence-preservation, consent, and recovery duties.

HO 24 71 modifies the policy to provide personal-liability coverage for bodily injury or property damage and medical-payments coverage arising from an insured's business pursuit, defined as a continuous, regular, or profit-motivated business activity conducted from the residence or elsewhere; it covers specified premises, insured acts, and legally responsible persons without making another person an insured.

HO 24 71 sets a $100,000 maximum for damages covered under the business-pursuits endorsement, applied to total damages regardless of the number of insureds, claimants, claims, or suits; the endorsement makes its coverage subject to and non-increasing of the personal-liability and medical-payments limits, and payment of the amount available under the limit ends the duty to defend and shifts further defense and settlement responsibility to the insured with reimbursement of reasonable defense expenses advanced afterward.

HO 24 73 modifies the policy for covered farming and farm premises, includes resident related household members and persons or organizations acting within the scope of duties performed for the insured in connection with covered farming, and grants bodily-injury/property-damage personal liability plus medical-payments coverage arising from covered personal activities, farming, or farm premises.

HO 24 73 applies the applicable personal-liability and medical-payments limits without stating a separate farm dollar limit in its cited grant, shares the limit across insureds and claimants, ends the defense after exhaustion, and retains business, professional-services, employee, workers-compensation, and business-animal exclusions.

HO 24 73 imposes farming-specific duties to maintain structures and animal controls, use care with agricultural materials and machinery, preserve operational records, report farm-operation claims, and notify the insurer of material changes, expansion, discontinuance, or transfer of control of the farming operation.

HO 24 82 modifies the policy by providing separate Personal Injury Coverage for an insured who is legally responsible for damages arising from covered offenses during the policy period, including false arrest, detention or imprisonment, malicious prosecution, wrongful eviction or entry, invasion of private occupancy, defamation, and privacy violations; the offense must arise from covered residence use or personal activities.

HO 24 82 excludes personal injury arising from business pursuits and business activities conducted from an insured location, except for activities ordinarily incidental to nonbusiness pursuits; its limit is one shared maximum for total covered personal-injury damages rather than a separate limit per insured, claimant, claim, or suit, approved settlement payments reduce the remaining amount, the attachment does not increase the limits of liability, and the preamble ends the defense duty when the applicable limit has been paid.

HO 04 96 is titled as a no-Section-II liability-coverages endorsement, but its supplied operative text grants personal liability, defense, and medical-payments coverage and then states an applicable limit shown in the Declarations for total occurrence damages; the supplied form text does not itself show an operative Section II deletion instruction, so the attached form, declarations, and controlling policy text must be reconciled before determining Section II availability.

Texas underwriting controls separately direct referral or non-acceptance for material business operations, agricultural activity, livestock, and certain animal exposures, and for premises used for business operations, professional services, production, farming, animal keeping, crop activity, or agricultural equipment; these are internal appetite controls rather than contractual coverage grants or exclusions.

The HO-4 2021-10 Coverage E pays damages for bodily injury or property damage caused by an occurrence and provides a defense by counsel of the insurer's choice; its business exclusion applies to business conducted from any location, its defense expenses and taxed costs are in addition to damages, and its own premises, vehicle, watercraft, property, rental, farming, and damages exclusions control the result.

The HO-6 2023-02 Coverage E pays damages for bodily injury or property damage caused by an occurrence and provides a defense against a covered suit; its business exclusion allows a result only when coverage is expressly provided by the policy, and its additional liability-related coverages remain separate and subject to their own exclusions, conditions, and duties.

The HO-3 2024-03, HO-4 2021-10, HO-5 2022-06, and HO-6 2023-02 base Coverage E grants address bodily injury and property damage rather than supplying the separate offense-based personal-injury grant provided by an attached HO 24 82 endorsement; a personal-injury allegation therefore requires review of the applicable attached endorsement and its exclusions.

The HO-3 2024-03, HO-4 2021-10, HO-5 2022-06, and HO-6 2023-02 base editions use the applicable liability limit rather than creating a new numeric limit in the Coverage E grant, apply coverage separately to insureds without increasing the occurrence limit, and end the defense duty on exhaustion; HO-4 additionally places defense expenses and taxed costs in addition to damages, while the other forms state their own requested-expense rules.

The liability claim-handling guidance is an internal workflow rather than contract language: after notice it directs file opening, party and policy identification, demand and service preservation, policy and endorsement review, investigation, defense coordination, authority-controlled resolution, recovery protection, and documented closure without amending the applicable policy.

The claims manual's liability chapter directs handlers to separate facts from allegations, preserve evidence, evaluate liability before stating a position, inspect property when useful, and refer serious, complex, intentional, criminal, governmental, professional-service, environmental, structural, product, or completed-work allegations; its 30-day notice screen is an internal handling control and does not replace the applicable policy's prompt-notice condition.

HO-5 2022-06 Coverage E provides bodily-injury and property-damage liability coverage and a defense, excludes business and business-pursuit exposures while preserving an incidental-to-nonbusiness exception, and Coverage F separately excludes bodily injury arising from a business; its Section II exclusions separately address business property, occasional rental up to fifteen days, professional services, business-entity roles, and vehicles, watercraft, and aircraft.

HO 04 48 (2026-06) changes Coverage B insurance for Other Structures and states that it does not change the property to which coverage applies while excluding other structures used in whole or in part for business purposes, farming, and certain rental uses; HO 04 65 (2018-09) changes Coverage C special limits, does not create coverage except as expressly provided, and leaves other coverage terms unchanged, so neither endorsement is a Section II liability grant.

HO 04 53 (2013-06) changes credit-card, fund-transfer-card, forgery, and counterfeit-loss coverage for direct financial loss, changes only the provisions it addresses, excludes loss from an insured's business activity, and applies a $10,000 total financial-loss limit; it is not business-pursuits liability or personal-injury coverage.

HO 04 91 (2019-03) provides HO-6 direct physical-loss coverage for covered property damaged by Water Backup with a $7,500 maximum, while HO 04 92 (2019-03) provides HO-4 direct physical-loss coverage for covered personal property damaged by water backup with a $2,500 maximum; these are property-loss endorsements, not liability or personal-injury grants.
